design.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 53-week trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to Cohort A (50 mg) or Cohort B (80 mg), each cohort further randomized 2:1 to olezarsen or matching placebo.

citations.quote: Trial CS3 was a 53-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial of adult subjects with FCS with fasting TG levels \ge 880 mg/dL despite very low-fat (\le 20 grams per day) diet and optimized lipid-lowering therapies.
Randomization: Randomly assigned to Cohort A (50 mg) or Cohort B (80 mg) in a 1:1 ratio; each cohort was further randomized 2:1 to either the olezarsen dose for the cohort or placebo

population.text: Adults with genetically confirmed familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) and fasting TG ≥ 880 mg/dL despite very low-fat diet and optimized lipid-lowering therapy.

citations.quote: Trial CS3 was a 53-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial of adult subjects with FCS with fasting TG levels \ge 880 mg/dL despite very low-fat (\le 20 grams per day) diet and optimized lipid-lowering therapies.

endpoint.text: Percent change in fasting triglycerides from baseline at Month 6 (average of Weeks 23, 25, and 27) for olezarsen 80 mg compared to placebo.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was change in fasting TG from baseline to Month 6 (defined as the average of Weeks 23, 25, and 27).
Percent change in fasting TG from baseline at Month 6 (average of Weeks 23, 25, and 27) for olezarsen 80 mg compared to placebo*

n.text: N=66 randomized (olezarsen 80 mg n=22; olezarsen 50 mg n=21; placebo n=23).

citations.quote: A total of 66 subjects were randomized to receive olezarsen (olezarsen 80 mg, n=22; olezarsen 50 mg, n=21) or placebo (n=23).

result.text: Olezarsen 80 mg reduced fasting TG at Month 6 by 44.5% relative to placebo (treatment difference -44.5, 95% CI -72.0, -17.0; p=0.0015); the 50 mg comparison was not significant (-21.5, 95% CI -48.2, 5.3; p=0.1153).

citations.quote: Olezarsen 80 mg administered every 4 weeks (as an add-on to background TG-lowering therapy) decreased TG at Month 6 by 44.5% compared to placebo.

indication.text: Adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS).

citations.quote: TRYNGOLZA is indicated as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS).

target_moa.text: An APOC-III-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) conjugated to triantennary N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc3) for hepatocyte delivery; it binds and causes degradation of apoC-III mRNA, reducing serum ApoC-III protein and lowering triglycerides.

citations.quote: Olezarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) inhibitor of apolipoprotein C-III (ApoC-III) production, covalently linked to a ligand containing three N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc) residues to enable delivery of the ASO to hepatocytes.
Olezarsen causes degradation of *apoC-III* mRNA through binding to *apoC-III* mRNA, which results in a reduction of serum ApoC-III protein.
TRYNGOLZA is an *APOC-III*-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) indicated as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS). (1)

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>5% and >3% higher than placebo) were injection site reactions (19% vs 9%), decreased platelet count (12% vs 4%), and arthralgia (9% vs 0%). Adverse reactions led to discontinuation in 7% of TRYNGOLZA-treated patients vs 0% placebo, most commonly hypersensitivity reactions.
